ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a benzene ring ortho-connected to a cyclization precursor containing N-H. The upper right of the benzene ring is connected to an O⁻ substituted carbon bearing a negative charge, and this carbon forms an alkene bond with the carbon on the right connected to R¹. The lower right of the benzene ring is connected to N-H, and N is further connected to the amide-like carbonyl carbon below; this carbonyl carbon is also connected to a methylene chain leading to R². The arrows in the figure show: the electrons of the upper O⁻ push back to form C=O, while the alkene-bond electrons move downward to form a new C-C bond to the lower carbonyl carbon, and the π electrons of the lower C=O transfer to oxygen. Reasoning: after simultaneous migration according to the arrows, the carbon where the upper original O⁻ was located becomes a carbonyl; the original alkene bond becomes a single bond and newly bonds with the lower carbonyl carbon, thereby closing the ring; the lower original carbonyl becomes an alcohol/alkoxide form and maintains its connections with N-H, the R² side chain, and the new C-C bond. Represent the R¹ and R² positions with the wildcard [*], and maintain the benzo N-H skeleton, obtaining the SMILES equivalent to this product as O=C1c2c(NC(C[*])(O)C1[*])cccc2.
